items.excerpt: NEJM AI reports the development and validation of an FDA-authorized AI/ML tool for predicting sepsis. (Date via Crossref created; ai.nejm.org is Cloudflare-gated, so product name and performance figures need confirming from the paper.)

items.title: ECG foundation models for cardiovascular screening in a cohort of young competitive athletes
items.excerpt: Three ECG foundation models (ECG-FM, HuBERT-ECG, ECGFounder) fine-tuned on 87,662 clinical ECGs were tested on 43 expert-annotated ECGs from national-level athletes, checking whether AI trained on general patients transfers to athlete pre-participation screening before deployment.

items.title: Explainable artificial intelligence for prehospital identification of endovascular thrombectomy candidates: a retrospective real-world study
items.excerpt: Using real-world EMS and hospital data from consecutive suspected-stroke transports, researchers built explainable machine-learning models to flag large-vessel-occlusion patients who need thrombectomy before hospital arrival, aiming to beat conventional prehospital stroke scales and cut transfer delays.

items.title: Multicenter evaluation of radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for colorectal cancer diagnosis and survival prediction
items.excerpt: Two-center retrospective study of 879 participants (741 locally advanced colorectal cancers, 138 benign lesions): clinical, radiomics, deep-learning and fusion models trained on pretreatment contrast CT at one center and tested at another; the clinical-radiomics nomogram reached a test AUC of 0.957.

items.title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer: a multicentre study
items.excerpt: Multicentre Lancet Digital Health study of a multimodal multitask deep-learning model that predicts tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer patients. (Date via Crossref created; article page blocked, figures need confirming.)

items.title: Bias and equity in large language model-based applications for health care: a scoping review
items.excerpt: Scoping review in The Lancet Digital Health mapping how bias and equity have been evaluated in LLM-based health-care applications. (Date via Crossref created.)

items.title: AI may not improve patient outcomes for stroke
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Hofstra/Northwell researchers compared 876 acute ischemic stroke patients before and after five AI tools went live at a comprehensive stroke center; CTA-within-60-minutes rose sharply, but odds of good functional outcome and discharge disposition did not change.

items.title: Will AI affect radiology malpractice cases?
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: in a randomized mock-jury experiment with 2,347 U.S. adults over a missed brain bleed, double reads, documented initial reads and disclosed AI error rates lowered perceived radiologist liability, but over 80% found the radiologist liable after switching a correct read to follow a wrong AI.

items.title: CT imaging biomarkers boost detection of early pancreatic cancer
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Johns Hopkins' TabMBio AI combines CT-derived tumor, pancreas and duct biomarkers with age and sex; on a 3,788-subject, 147-center benchmark it hit AUC 0.99 for sub-2 cm cancers and lifted sensitivity on prediagnostic CTs from 19.5% to 29.3%.

items.title: New AI guidance to cut paperwork and free more time for care
items.excerpt: UK government issues national guidance on adopting AI in adult social care; a Swindon pilot cut social workers' admin time 63% and Care Act assessment conversations from 1.5 hours to 30 minutes.

items.title: Zimmer submits Monogram robot to FDA
items.excerpt: Zimmer Biomet filed a 90-day 510(k) for the autonomous, CT-guided Monogram knee-replacement robot with hands-free automated bone cutting, targeting a 2027 launch; no safety events were reported in its clinical trial.

items.title: 진단만 하는 AI 넘어섰다…자율 의료 AI 에이전트, 검사·처방·입원 결정까지 수행
items.excerpt: Heidelberg/TU Dresden's autonomous agent MIRA ran a virtual ED (interview, tests, diagnosis, prescribing, admission) on 574 real patient cases; on 311 shared cases it reached 87.8% diagnostic accuracy vs 78.1% for specialists, per a Nature paper. Part of Medigate's 2026 notable-papers relay; Nature paper date not verified.

items.title: AI health chatbot shows no benefit for perinatal anxiety or depression
items.excerpt: Randomized trial of 400 pregnant/postpartum racial and ethnic minority participants (JAMA Network Open) found a generative-AI health chatbot did not change anxiety, depression, ED visits, postpartum care or sleep vs control. (Off-list source; underlying JAMA Netw Open paper online 2026-11-04 per Crossref.)

items.title: AI imaging reports comparable to the work of sonographers and cardiologists
items.excerpt: In a randomized trial of AI- versus human-generated preliminary reports for 1,200 echocardiograms, blinded cardiologists edited 50.6% of AI reports and 49.7% of human reports, meeting noninferiority.

items.title: Epic Systems defends competitive practices, promises to let AI access its records
items.excerpt: Epic executives at HLTH defended the EHR giant's competitive practices and pledged to let third-party AI tools access patient records held in its system.

items.title: Medicare Pays For the AI Eye Scan — Nobody Pays For What Comes Next
items.excerpt: Medicare reimburses autonomous AI diabetic-retinopathy screening, but follow-up care after a positive result is unfunded, which shapes every other barrier to deployment (opinion).

items.title: Recursion REC-4881 Phase 3 design aligned with FDA in FAP
items.excerpt: Recursion agreed with FDA on a registrational Phase 3 design for its AI-platform-derived MEK1/2 inhibitor REC-4881 in familial adenomatous polyposis; the ~200-patient trial is slated for H2 2027. (Off-list source: on-list outlets had no fresh coverage.)
